what: first v2 experiment: with STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR on, the router's own top-10 is dead work; implemented an opt-in skip, proved exactness analytically, gated on paired cells - REJECTED

change.what: when the route prior is active (512 experts, k=10, residency table present) the prior re-picks the top-10 from the same logits and overwrites ids/weights, so native_router_top10_multi's selection is dead; the skip drops that one launch per layer
change.exactness: PROVEN by inspection: route_prior_k reads only logits and res; ids/weights are write-only outputs. A same-process trace comparison was not possible; the cross-process --dump-routing comparison differed only because the two runs took different trajectories (99 vs 93 drafts, the known greedy restart drift)

r31g.note: the trace cells failed (--dump-routing was passed to env, rc=127) so the window verdict was a false-negative NOT ADOPTED

r31h.trace: byte-differ at 232761 due to trajectory drift, not the change

verdict: REJECTED (not adopted): 1K median +1.31% with 3/5 wins misses the pre-declared >=+2.0% / 4-of-5 gate; 32K and 128K are inside the trajectory band (accepted counts swing 197<->207 and 24<->32). The redundancy is real but worth <2% - the native multi top-10 is one cheap launch per layer.
next: the runner-up experiment (batch the small GEMV calls z/rec/ab + shared into fewer launches) is the remaining defensible candidate at ~1.7-2.9%; no other single bounded change clears the gate on the current profile
